acceptance: The exact implementation changes only crates/morize-core/src/digest.rs and crates/morize-core/src/lib.rs.
morize-core exports public Sha256Digest and DigestParseError values plus SHA256_DIGEST_BYTE_LENGTH = 32 and SHA256_DIGEST_TEXT_LENGTH = 64.
Sha256Digest stores exactly 32 opaque bytes and provides const from_bytes, as_bytes, and into_bytes operations that preserve those bytes exactly.
Display emits exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal ASCII characters with no prefix, separators, normalization, truncation, or alternate representation.
FromStr accepts exactly the canonical 64-byte lowercase hexadecimal representation and reconstructs the exact original 32 bytes.
Parsing rejects any input whose UTF-8 byte length is not exactly 64 with DigestParseError::InvalidLength { actual }.
Parsing rejects uppercase hexadecimal and every other non-canonical byte with DigestParseError::NonCanonicalHex { index, byte } at the exact offending byte position.
DigestParseError is bounded metadata-only and never carries the source string or digest bytes.
Sha256Digest supports Clone, Copy, Eq, PartialEq, Ord, PartialOrd, and Hash value semantics; Debug does not disclose the digest bytes or canonical digest text.
Focused deterministic tests cover all 256 repeated-byte patterns for bytes -> canonical text -> parse -> bytes round trips and representative non-canonical ASCII at every canonical text position.

This Grain defines only an algorithm-specific SHA-256 digest value representation; it does not compute SHA-256, canonicalize content bytes, authenticate content, prove authority, or establish collision/preimage/security claims.

The implementation defines no blob store, content-addressed path builder, evidence-chain logic, idempotency behavior, serialization framework integration, persisted/wire schema, migration, storage, API, MCP, retrieval, or domain-record integration.
cargo fmt --all -- --check passes on the exact implementation head.
cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline passes on the exact implementation head.
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --offline -- -D warnings passes on the exact implementation head.
cargo test --workspace --all-targets --offline passes and executes the focused SHA-256 digest value/parser tests.
Cargo manifests and Cargo.lock are unchanged; the Grain adds no runtime, build, dev, or test dependency.
GitHub Actions passes Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows on the exact implementation head before acceptance.

An independent semantic reviewer reviews the exact implementation head for SHA-256 value-width semantics, strict canonical text parsing, metadata-only errors, non-disclosing Debug behavior, no hashing/security overclaim, scope containment, prerequisite identity, and required evidence.
ADR-0004 proof prerequisite SG-000011 revalidates against the exact WorkPacket baseline before execution.

method.control: Implementation is limited to one dependency-free SHA-256 digest value/parser module, focused deterministic tests, and morize-core re-exports. No SHA-256 computation, canonical-content encoder, blob addressing, persistence, serialization, authority semantics, or third-party dependency is authorized.
method.review_separation: An independent semantic reviewer must review the exact implementation head for exact 32-byte SHA-256 value semantics, strict lowercase canonical parser behavior, metadata-only errors, non-disclosing Debug behavior, absence of hashing/security overclaims, prerequisite identity, scope containment, and required evidence separately from the implementing agent before acceptance.
method.rollback: Revert the SG-000025 digest value implementation commits; no persisted format, hash computation, blob path, migration, or user data depends on this Grain.

minimality.rationale: The narrowest P1 content-identity increment is an algorithm-specific value type for the SHA-256 bytes and canonical text already implied by the architecture's blobs/sha256 layout. Separating representation from hash computation avoids prematurely coupling the core to a cryptographic dependency or canonical-content encoding before those contracts receive their own Grains.

requirements: Parsing must fail closed on non-canonical length, uppercase hexadecimal, or any other non-lowercase-hex byte; no normalization or truncation is permitted.
Debug and parse errors must not disclose digest bytes or source text because content fingerprints can become sensitive metadata.
The type must not imply that arbitrary bytes supplied through from_bytes were actually produced by SHA-256 or that digest equality establishes authority, trust, authenticity, or operation identity.

outcome: morize-core exposes one dependency-free Sha256Digest value with exact 32-byte semantics and one strict lowercase 64-character canonical text representation, without yet computing hashes, canonicalizing content, adding persistence/serialization, or introducing dependencies.
rationale: P1 requires stable content digests; docs/DATA_MODEL.md says exact content identity uses a cryptographic digest over canonical bytes, while docs/ARCHITECTURE.md fixes the v1 blob namespace as blobs/sha256. This Grain defines only the SHA-256 digest value/text contract so later hashing and canonical-byte Grains can depend on an explicit typed representation without conflating digest bytes with authority, operation identity, or persistence semantics.

risk.recovery: Revert the SG-000025 digest value implementation commits; no persisted format, hash computation, blob path, migration, or user data has been written by this Grain.

scope_in: Define public Sha256Digest as exactly 32 opaque bytes with const from_bytes, as_bytes, and into_bytes accessors.
Define strict canonical lowercase hexadecimal Display and FromStr behavior over exactly 64 ASCII bytes with bounded DigestParseError variants for invalid length and the first non-canonical byte.
Provide deterministic Clone/Copy/Eq/Ord/Hash value semantics while ensuring Debug does not reveal the digest bytes or canonical digest text.
Add dependency-free focused tests including all 256 repeated-byte round trips and representative non-canonical ASCII rejection at every canonical text byte position.
scope_out: Computing SHA-256 from raw or canonical content bytes, incremental hashing, streaming readers, hardware acceleration, digest verification helpers, collision/preimage claims, digital signatures, MACs, authentication, trust, or authority semantics.

Canonical serialization/content-byte definition, Unicode normalization, domain-record encoding, blob path derivation, content-addressed storage, evidence-ledger chaining, idempotency keys, mutation compare-and-swap, or operation identity.
Serde or other serialization-framework integration, persisted/wire schema, vault format, migration, configuration, APIs, MCP, retrieval, connectors, or domain memory records.
Any runtime, build, dev, or test dependency.
